statement: TSMC is reported to be outsourcing a key CoWoS front-end step to OSAT partners as NVIDIA reserves roughly 800,000-850,000 wafers of 2026 CoWoS capacity (over half the year's total), with the CoWoS supply-demand gap still estimated at about 20% in 2026 despite monthly capacity rising from ~70,000 wafers in 2025 to 130,000-140,000 by end-2026.
why: Advanced packaging is the physical bottleneck for AI accelerators: even after roughly doubling monthly capacity and pushing work out to outside assembly houses, orders still exceed what can be packaged, so shipments stay capacity-rationed and NVIDIA's booking of more than half the pool squeezes everyone else.

impact.mechanism: CoWoS packaging capacity gates how many GPU and custom-ASIC modules with stacked memory can be built; a persistent gap between reserved demand and available capacity caps unit shipments even as capacity expands.

evidence.excerpt: the report estimates that the CoWoS supply-demand gap will remain at approximately 20% in 2026
NVIDIA has reportedly reserved approximately 800,000 to 850,000 wafers of TSMC's CoWoS capacity for 2026
TSMC's monthly CoWoS capacity is projected to increase from approximately 70,000 wafers in 2025 to 130,000-140,000 wafers by the end of 2026

confidence.basis: Secondary trade-research write-up citing other outlets (ETNews, Mydrivers, Mirror Daily) rather than separately fetched primary sources; figures are reported estimates, not TSMC disclosure.

dispersion: NVIDIA reservation quoted as a range of 800,000-850,000 wafers; end-2026 monthly capacity as 130,000-140,000 wafers.
